title: Transmission warning light on
h1: Why is my transmission warning light on?
metaDesc: Transmission light or transmission temperature warning on? Answer a few questions to see if it's overheating, low fluid or a fault, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: transmission light came on and car wont shift
intro: A transmission warning usually means one of two things: the transmission fluid is getting too hot, or the transmission computer has found a fault. Overheating needs you to stop and let it cool. A fault often puts the car into a backup mode with one gear. How the car is driving tells us which one you're dealing with.
safety: If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
If the car suddenly loses drive in traffic, turn on your hazard lights and coast to the shoulder.
If the engine temperature warning is on as well, stop and turn the engine off.

q_driving.q: How is the car driving right now?
q_driving.help: "Slipping" means the engine revs rise but the car doesn't speed up to match, as if it's briefly in neutral.

opts.a: It won't move, barely moves, or the engine revs but the car doesn't go
There's a burning smell, smoke, or red fluid dripping
It's stuck in one gear: slow to pick up speed and won't shift up
It drives normally. Only the light or message is on

q_which_light.help: Your owner's manual shows each symbol. A thermometer means temperature. A gear shape with an exclamation mark, or a flashing gear letter, usually means a fault.

opts.a: A temperature warning: a thermometer, "Trans Temp", "AT Oil Temp" or "Transmission Hot"
A gear symbol with an exclamation mark, "Service/Check Transmission", or a flashing gear letter or O/D OFF light

q_temp_when.q: What was happening when the temperature warning came on?

opts.a: Towing, carrying a heavy load, climbing a long hill, or creeping in hot stop-and-go traffic
The engine temperature gauge is high too
Normal driving, with no heavy load

result.title: The transmission has lost drive. Don't try to force it
result.now: Put the car in Park, set the parking brake and turn the engine off. Have it towed to a shop.
if: If you're in traffic, turn on your hazard lights and let the car roll to the shoulder if you can.
If you find a large puddle of red fluid under the car, tell the tow company and the shop. A leak may be the whole problem.
If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
result.why: When the engine revs but the car won't move, the transmission isn't connecting the engine to the wheels. Running it like this can turn a smaller problem, like low fluid, into a much bigger repair.

causes.name: Very low transmission fluid from a leak
causes.clues: Red or brown fluid under the car, or slipping that got worse over a few days.

causes.name: Internal transmission failure
causes.clues: Slipping, harsh shifts or a burning smell in the days before.

causes.name: Broken shift cable or linkage
causes.clues: The shifter moves freely or feels disconnected, and the gear display doesn't change.
causes.against: If the gear display changes and you feel a clunk going into gear, a linkage problem is less likely.

you: Look under the car for red or brown fluid.
Check whether the gear display changes when you move the shifter.
shop: Transmission fluid level and condition check

result.title: Fluid may be leaking onto hot parts, or the transmission is overheating badly
result.now: Pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off and get out of the car if you see smoke. Have it towed.
if: If there are flames or the smoke keeps growing, move well away and call 911.
If you see smoke or flames, don't open the hood: get everyone away from the car and call 911. Let the fire service deal with it.
If the smell fades once it cools, it still needs a leak inspection before you drive it again.
result.why: Transmission fluid burns and smokes when it hits the exhaust or gets far too hot. Either way, the transmission is losing fluid or being damaged, and leaking fluid near hot parts is a fire risk.

causes.name: Leaking transmission cooler line or seal
causes.clues: Red fluid dripping, or wet spots along the lines that run toward the radiator.

causes.name: Severely overheated, slipping transmission
causes.clues: Slipping or a flaring engine speed before the smell started.

causes.name: Leaking pan gasket or axle seal
causes.clues: Fluid near the bottom of the transmission or at the inner end of a front axle.

shop: Transmission fluid level and condition check

result.title: The transmission may be in backup (limp) mode because of a fault
result.now: Get off busy roads and highways as soon as it's safe and have it towed. Limp mode can let go without warning.
if: If it starts slipping, smells burnt, shows smoke or won't move, stop and have it towed.
If turning the car off and back on makes it shift normally, the fault is still stored and can return without warning. Get it scanned within a few days and avoid highways until then.
If the engine temperature gauge is high or the check engine light is flashing, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: When the transmission computer sees a problem, it often locks the transmission in one gear to protect it. That's why the car feels sluggish and won't shift up. The stored code points the shop to the right area to test.

causes.name: Shift solenoid or speed sensor fault
causes.clues: It went into one gear suddenly, with no slipping first.

causes.name: Low or burnt transmission fluid
causes.clues: Slipping or harsh shifts in recent weeks, or a leak.

causes.name: Wiring, connector or low battery voltage
causes.clues: Other warning lights came on at the same time, or the battery is weak.

you: Look under the car for red fluid.
Note whether other warning lights came on at the same time.

result.title: The transmission fluid may have got too hot from the extra work
result.now: Pull over where it's safe, shift into Park and let the engine idle until the warning goes out, unless your owner's manual says to do something different. Don't continue towing or carrying the heavy load until the transmission has been checked.
if: If the warning doesn't go out after 15–20 minutes, or comes back soon after, have it towed.
If it happens again under the same load, have the fluid and cooling checked. You may be near the limit of what the car is built to tow or carry.
If you smell burning, see smoke, the car slips or the engine temperature gauge is high too, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: Towing, heavy loads, long climbs and slow traffic in the heat all make the transmission work harder and heat its fluid. Idling in Park lets the fluid circulate and cool. Very hot fluid wears out quickly, so it's worth having it checked afterward.

causes.name: Heavy load or towing beyond what the cooling can handle
causes.clues: It only happens when towing or loaded, especially uphill or on hot days.

causes.name: Low or old transmission fluid
causes.clues: The fluid hasn't been changed in a long time, or there's a leak.

causes.name: Clutch overheating (dual-clutch transmissions)
causes.clues: Creeping in traffic or holding the car on a hill with the gas pedal.

you: Check your owner's manual for the towing limit and the right warning procedure.
Look under the car for leaks once it's parked.
shop: Transmission fluid level and condition check

result.title: The transmission may be running hot without an obvious reason
result.now: Pull over where it's safe, shift into Park and let it idle until the warning goes out. Have the transmission checked before relying on the car, and have it towed if the warning comes back.
if: If the warning comes back on a normal drive, have it towed instead of driving it again.
If the car slips, shifts harshly, smells burnt or you see smoke, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
If the engine temperature gauge is high too, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and don't restart it.
result.why: Normal driving shouldn't overheat a healthy transmission. When it does, common causes are fluid that's low or worn out, the cooler is blocked, or the transmission is slipping inside and making extra heat.

causes.name: Low transmission fluid
causes.clues: Red spots where you park, or slipping when cold.

causes.name: Blocked transmission cooler or damaged cooler lines
causes.clues: Debris in front of the radiator, or a recent front-end bump.

causes.name: Slipping inside the transmission
causes.clues: Engine revs flaring between shifts.

causes.name: Faulty temperature sensor
causes.clues: The warning comes on right after a cold start.
causes.against: If the car shifts and drives perfectly, a sensor fault becomes more likely, but a shop should confirm the real temperature with a scan tool before you rely on that.

you: Look for red fluid where you park.
Check in front of the radiator for leaves, bags or debris.
shop: Transmission fluid level and condition check
Transmission temperature reading with a scan tool

result.title: The engine may be overheating and heating the transmission too
result.now: Pull over where it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't open the radiator cap while it's hot. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see steam or smell sweet coolant, stay away from the hood until it cools.
If the temperature gauge was in the red, don't restart the engine to "get it home". Overheating can damage the engine quickly.
If you smell burning or see smoke rather than steam, step away from the car.
result.why: On many cars, the transmission fluid is cooled by the engine's radiator. When the engine overheats, the transmission does too. The engine problem is the one to deal with first.

causes.name: Engine cooling problem (low coolant, fan, thermostat, water pump)
causes.clues: The engine temperature gauge is high, steam, or a sweet smell.

causes.name: Blocked radiator
causes.clues: Debris in front of the radiator, or towing in very hot weather.

you: Once fully cool, check the coolant level in the see-through reservoir.
Look for coolant puddles under the front of the car.

result.title: The transmission computer has found a fault
result.now: Have the transmission codes read within the next few days. Until then, drive gently and avoid towing or heavy loads.
if: If the car starts slipping, shifting harshly or gets stuck in one gear, avoid highways and get it checked right away rather than waiting.
If the light is flashing and the car won't shift at all, have it towed.
If you smell burning, see smoke or the engine temperature gauge is high, pull over, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: This light means the transmission computer has stored a fault, even if you can't feel a problem yet. Faults caught early are often a sensor, solenoid or low fluid, and a shop will usually test those before suggesting bigger repairs. Driving on them can lead to bigger damage.

causes.name: Speed sensor or shift solenoid fault
causes.clues: Shifts feel slightly late or firm, or the speedometer flickers.

causes.name: Low or worn-out fluid
causes.clues: It's been a long time since the fluid was changed, or there's a leak.

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem
causes.clues: The light comes and goes, especially over bumps or in wet weather.

you: Look for red fluid where you park.
Note when the light comes on and how the shifts feel.
shop: Transmission code scan (needs a tool that reads the transmission computer)

result.title: Treat it as a transmission fault and get it scanned
result.now: Look up the light in your owner's manual. If it's a temperature warning, pull over and let it idle in Park until it goes out. Either way, get the codes read within a few days.
if: If the car slips, won't shift, smells burnt or you see smoke, stop driving it and have it towed.
If the engine temperature gauge is high as well, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and don't restart it.
result.why: Transmission warnings cover overheating and electrical faults, and they're handled differently. Your owner's manual will tell you which one you're seeing, and a scan will show why.

causes.name: Transmission fluid overheating
causes.clues: A thermometer symbol, towing, hills or heavy traffic.

causes.name: Transmission sensor or solenoid fault
causes.clues: A gear symbol or a flashing gear letter.

you: Take a photo of the warning to show the shop.
Look for red fluid under the car.
